claims.evidence: Behavioral data show that mutants of Or67d, lush, and snmp exhibited similar post-stimulus aggregation to wild-type (Figure 2—figure supplement 4, p = 0.4405).

claims.claim: Hexane can extract the active pheromone off the glass surface in the food-odor-induced quadrant.
claims.source: Since most insect pheromones are lipophilic carbohydrates dissolvable in hexane (van der Goes van Naters and Carlson, 2007), we reasoned that hexane might extract the active pheromone off the glass surface in the food-odor-induced quadrant.
claims.evidence: This is supported by behavioral experiments showing that naïve flies could trace and follow an 'E' pattern painted with hexane extracts from pheromone-deposited glass plates (Figure 3A, B, Video 3).

claims.claim: Naïve flies can trace and follow patterns painted with hexane extracts of pheromone deposits.
claims.source: We induced wild-type flies to deposit the food-odor induced pheromone onto the glass plate and dissolved the deposited molecules into hexane. We then painted the hexane extract onto a new glass plate in a letter 'E' pattern. Naïve new flies were able to trace and follow the E pattern but do not follow control hexane extracts of flies stimulated by humidified air painted in the same pattern (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Video 3).
claims.evidence: Behavioral tracking data show flies following the 'E' pattern painted with pheromone extract but not control extract (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Video 3).

claims.claim: The pheromone is volatile.
claims.source: Behavioral results suggested the pheromone was volatile because: 1) it required the olfactory system for detection (Figure 2C); 2) constant air flushing reduced behavioral attraction after ∼25 min (Figure 1—figure supplement 5); and 3) heating the pheromone-containing arena to 32°C to increase odor volatility eliminated post-stimulus behaviors (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Multiple lines of evidence support volatility: requirement for olfactory system, reduction over time with air flushing, and elimination of behavior with heating.

claims.claim: cVA was not detected in pheromone extracts from the glass plates.
claims.source: Consistent with behavioral results that cVA is unlikely to be the food-odor induced pheromone (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), cVA was not detected in pheromone extracts from the glass plates (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: GC-MS analysis of hexane extracts did not detect cVA (Supplementary file 1).

claims.claim: 7-docosene and 23-methyldocosane were not detected in pheromone extracts.
claims.source: 7-docosene and 23-methyldocosane were also not detected, while 5-tricosene was detected at trace amounts (Figure 3C and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: GC-MS analysis results (Figure 3C, Supplementary file 1).

claims.claim: 5-tricosene was detected at trace amounts in pheromone extracts.
claims.source: 7-docosene and 23-methyldocosane were also not detected, while 5-tricosene was detected at trace amounts (Figure 3C and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: GC-MS analysis results (Figure 3C, Supplementary file 1).

claims.claim: Levels of 7-tricosene were increased in the experimental conditions but behavioral results excluded it as the food-odor-induced pheromone.
claims.source: The levels of 7-tricosene were increased in the experimental conditions. However, our behavioral results excluded 7-tricosene as the food-odor-induced pheromone (Figure 2B; also see below and Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: GC-MS showed increased 7-tricosene, but ppk23 mutants (which cannot detect 7-tricosene) showed normal aggregation (Figure 2B), and 7-tricosene induced neutral to slightly repulsive behavior (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene was significantly enriched in the experimental but not humidified air + flies control group.
claims.source: Interestingly, only one other peak was significantly enriched in the experimental but not humidified air + flies control group: (Z) 9-tricosene (9-T) (Figure 3C, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: GC-MS analysis showed 9-tricosene exhibited a 2.8 fold enrichment on glass plates upon food-odor stimulation (Figure 3C, Supplementary file 1).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene is a male-specific volatile pheromone in D. melanogaster.
claims.source: Little is known regarding the function of 9-tricosene in D. melanogaster besides its presence as a male-specific volatile pheromone (Everaerts et al., 2010; Farine et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies identifying 9-tricosene as male-specific and volatile (Everaerts et al., 2010; Farine et al., 2012).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene elicits attraction behaviors in Drosophila.
claims.source: To determine if 9-tricosene was attractive to Drosophila, as would be predicted for the food-odor induced aggregation pheromone, we used 9-tricosene as the stimulus in the 4-field olfactory assay. Indeed, 9-tricosene elicits attraction behaviors (Figure 3D-E, Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show dose-dependent attraction to 9-tricosene (Figure 3D-E).

claims.claim: Naïve flies trace and follow 9-tricosene patterns, paying particular attention to the odor border.
claims.source: To determine if 9-tricosene could direct aggregation behaviors, we repeated the 'E' experiment using 9-tricosene alone (Figure 3F). Naïve flies did trace and follow the 9-tricosene pattern, paying particular attention to the odor border (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: Behavioral tracking data show flies following 9-tricosene 'E' pattern with preference for borders (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).

claims.claim: Flies appear to be repelled by the center of a concentrated 9-tricosene odor trail.
claims.source: Nonetheless, the aggregation response was not identical to the full hexane extract. In particular, flies appeared to be repelled by the center of a concentrated 9-tricosene odor trail.
claims.evidence: Behavioral observations from the 'E' pattern experiment (Figure 3F) show flies avoiding the center of concentrated 9-tricosene deposits.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene under certain conditions can function as an aggregation pheromone, although additional pheromone components may contribute to the full aggregation phenotype.
claims.source: Overall, these data suggest that 9-tricosene under certain conditions can function as an aggregation pheromone, although additional pheromone components may contribute to the full aggregation phenotype.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation that 9-tricosene alone shows some but not all characteristics of the full pheromone extract in behavioral assays.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene and other cuticular hydrocarbons are produced by oenocytes on the fly abdominal wall.
claims.source: 9-Tricosene is a member of cuticular hydrocarbons produced by oenocytes on the fly abdominal wall (Billeter et al., 2009; Everaerts et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies showing oenocytes produce cuticular hydrocarbons including 9-tricosene (Billeter et al., 2009; Everaerts et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Oenocyte-less males mixed with wild-type females no longer produced post-stimulus aggregation behavior.
claims.source: Oenocyte-less males mixed with wild-type females no longer produced a post-stimulus aggregation behavior, suggesting that an oenocyte-derived cuticular hydrocarbon is essential for post-stimulus aggregation (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show reduced post-stimulus aggregation when oenocyte-ablated males were used as depositors (Figure 3—figure supplement 4, p = 0.0021).

claims.claim: An oenocyte-derived cuticular hydrocarbon is essential for post-stimulus aggregation.
claims.source: Oenocyte-less males mixed with wild-type females no longer produced a post-stimulus aggregation behavior, suggesting that an oenocyte-derived cuticular hydrocarbon is essential for post-stimulus aggregation (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the observation that ablating oenocytes, which produce cuticular hydrocarbons including 9-tricosene, eliminates post-stimulus aggregation.

claims.claim: The orco mutants completely lacked responses to 9-tricosene in electroantennogram recordings.
claims.source: The orco mutants completely lacked responses to 9-tricosene (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—source data 1). This suggests that 9-tricosene activates an orco-dependent odorant receptor, and does not require signaling from Ir or Gr receptors.
claims.evidence: EAG recordings show no response to 9-tricosene in orco mutants compared to wild-type (Figure 4A,B).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene activates an orco-dependent odorant receptor and does not require signaling from Ir or Gr receptors.
claims.source: The orco mutants completely lacked responses to 9-tricosene (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—source data 1). This suggests that 9-tricosene activates an orco-dependent odorant receptor, and does not require signaling from Ir or Gr receptors.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on EAG data showing complete loss of 9-tricosene response in orco mutants.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene elicits rapid and robust firing patterns in the antennal basiconic ab4 sensillum.
claims.source: We found that 9-tricosene elicits rapid and robust firing patterns in the antennal basiconic ab4 sensillum, which houses two neurons (ab4A and ab4B) that express Or7a (ab4A) or Or56a receptors (ab4B) (Figure 4C) (Couto et al., 2005; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Stensmyr et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data show robust responses to 9-tricosene in ab4 sensilla (Figure 4C).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene stimulates spiking of the larger amplitude neuron in ab4 sensillum, indicating the 9-tricosene-responsive ORNs are ab4A, which express Or7a receptors.
claims.source: 9-Tricosene stimulates spiking of the larger amplitude neuron indicating the 9-tricosene-responsive ORNs are ab4A, which express Or7a receptors.
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording traces show activation of the larger amplitude spike in ab4 sensilla upon 9-tricosene stimulation (Figure 4D).

claims.claim: Stimulation of ab4 sensilla by flies pre-stimulated with apple cider vinegar led to significant increases in ab4A (Or7a) activation compared to flies pre-stimulated with dry air.
claims.source: Stimulation of ab4 sensilla by flies housed in a glass vial pre-stimulated with apple cider vinegar, compared to flies pre-stimulated with dry air alone, also led to significant increases in ab4A (Or7a) activation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data show increased ab4 spike frequency when stimulated with flies pre-exposed to apple cider vinegar versus dry air (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, p = 0.03).

claims.claim: Or7a is a broadly tuned receptor that responds to a broad range of odors, including many aldehydes and alcohols.
claims.source: The identification of Or7a as a 9-tricosene pheromone receptor was surprising as, unlike previously identified pheromone receptors, it had been shown to respond to a broad range of odors, including many aldehydes and alcohols (Hallem et al., 2004; Hallem and Carlson, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to comprehensive studies characterizing Or7a responses to multiple odorants (Hallem et al., 2004; Hallem and Carlson, 2006).

claims.claim: Expression of Or7a in ab3A neurons endows them the ability to respond to 9-tricosene comparable to endogenous Or7a-positive ab4 sensillum.
claims.source: To determine if the Or7a receptor is sufficient for 9-tricosene responses, we misexpressed Or7a in an olfactory neuron that lacks an odorant receptor in ab3A sensillar neurons (Dobritsa et al., 2003). Expression of Or7a endowed ab3A neurons the ability to respond to 9-tricosene comparable to the 9-tricosene activation pattern detected in endogenous Or7a-positive ab4 sensillum (Figure 4D,E).
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data show that ab3 neurons expressing Or7a respond to 9-tricosene similarly to native ab4 neurons (Figure 4D,E).

claims.claim: The Or7a receptor responds to 9-tricosene.
claims.source: These data indicate that the Or7a receptor responds to 9-tricosene.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on data showing Or7a is necessary (Or7a mutants lack response) and sufficient (misexpression confers response) for 9-tricosene detection.

claims.claim: Basiconic sensilla were traditionally considered food odor detectors.
claims.source: This is unexpected since basiconic sensilla were traditionally considered food odor detectors (Larsson et al., 2004; Suh et al., 2004; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Jones et al., 2007; Laissue and Vosshall, 2008).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies characterizing basiconic sensilla as responding to food odors.

claims.claim: Both male and female ab4A/Or7a neurons responded equally to 9-tricosene.
claims.source: Both male and female ab4A/Or7a neurons responded equally to 9-tricosene (Figure 4E), consistent with 9-tricosene being attractive to both males and females (Figure 1—figure supplement 8).
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data show similar responses to 9-tricosene in male and female ab4 neurons (Figure 4E).

claims.claim: Or7a neurons did not respond to cVA.
claims.source: Or7a neurons did not respond to cVA (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data show no significant response of ab4 sensilla to various concentrations of cVA (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claims.claim: No spontaneous or 9-tricosene stimulated ab4A spiking activity was observed in Or7a mutant flies.
claims.source: Ab4 sensilla in Or7a mutants were identified based on their shape and the specific response of the ab4B neuron to geosmin (Stensmyr et al., 2012). No spontaneous or 9-tricosene stimulated ab4A spiking activity was observed in Or7a mutant flies (Figure 4F,G), indicating that Or7a is necessary for 9-tricosene activation in ab4 sensilla.
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data show complete loss of ab4A response to 9-tricosene in Or7a mutants while ab4B response to geosmin remains intact (Figure 4F,G).

claims.claim: Or7a is necessary for 9-tricosene activation in ab4 sensilla.
claims.source: No spontaneous or 9-tricosene stimulated ab4A spiking activity was observed in Or7a mutant flies (Figure 4F,G), indicating that Or7a is necessary for 9-tricosene activation in ab4 sensilla.
claims.evidence: Single sensillum recording data from Or7a mutants show no ab4A response to 9-tricosene (Figure 4F,G).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene specifically activates the 'generalist' Or7a receptor.
claims.source: All together, these data suggest that 9-tricosene specifically activates the 'generalist' Or7a receptor.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on electrophysiological data showing Or7a is necessary and sufficient for 9-tricosene responses, combined with previous knowledge that Or7a responds to many odorants.

claims.claim: Or7a-GAL4 specifically drives effector expression only in olfactory neurons that target the DL5 antennal lobe glomerulus.
claims.source: Or7a-GAL4 specifically drives effector expression only in olfactory neurons that target the DL5 antennal lobe glomerulus (Figure 5A) (Couto et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Immunostaining data show Or7a-expressing neurons innervating the DL5 glomerulus (Figure 5A), consistent with previous characterization (Couto et al., 2005).

claims.claim: Or7a expression was not detected outside the antennae.
claims.source: We did not detect expression outside the antennae (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Imaging of Or7a-GAL4 expression in whole animals, dissected brain and ventral nerve cord showed expression only in antennal olfactory neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: Aggregation responses to naturally deposited food-odor induced pheromone were completely abolished in Or7a neuron-ablated flies.
claims.source: Aggregation responses to both the naturally deposited food-odor induced pheromone (Figure 5B,C, Figure 5—source data 1) and to 9-tricosene (Figure 5D,E) were completely abolished in Or7a neuron-ablated flies obtained using Or7a-Gal4+UAS-hid (Figure 5) or Or7a-Gal4+UAS-DTI (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or7a neuron-ablated flies (Or7a-Gal4/UAS-hid) had significantly reduced post-stimulus aggregation to natural pheromone (Figure 5B,C, p = 0.0012) and to 9-tricosene (Figure 5D,E, p < 0.001).

claims.claim: Aggregation responses to 9-tricosene were completely abolished in Or7a neuron-ablated flies.
claims.source: Aggregation responses to both the naturally deposited food-odor induced pheromone (Figure 5B,C, Figure 5—source data 1) and to 9-tricosene (Figure 5D,E) were completely abolished in Or7a neuron-ablated flies obtained using Or7a-Gal4+UAS-hid (Figure 5) or Or7a-Gal4+UAS-DTI (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or7a neuron-ablated flies had no attraction to 9-tricosene (Figure 5D,E; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).

claims.claim: Ablation of other odorant receptors (OrX-Gal4+UAS-hid) did not affect aggregation.
claims.source: Ablation of other odorant receptors (OrX-Gal4+UAS-hid) did not affect aggregation (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show that ablation of Or83c, Or43a, and Or88a neurons did not significantly affect post-stimulus aggregation (Figure 5C).

claims.claim: Or7a mutants completely lacked attraction to the naturally deposited food-odor-induced pheromone.
claims.source: Similarly, Or7a mutants completely lacked attraction to the naturally deposited food-odor-induced pheromone and to 9-tricosene (Figure 5B-E).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or7a mutants had significantly reduced post-stimulus aggregation to natural pheromone (Figure 5B,C, p = 0.006) and to 9-tricosene (Figure 5D,E).

claims.claim: Or7a mutants completely lacked attraction to 9-tricosene.
claims.source: Similarly, Or7a mutants completely lacked attraction to the naturally deposited food-odor-induced pheromone and to 9-tricosene (Figure 5B-E).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or7a mutants had no significant attraction to 9-tricosene (Figure 5D,E).

claims.claim: 7-tricosene induced a neutral to slightly repulsive behavior in wild-type flies.
claims.source: To verify that aggregation behavior is specific to 9-tricosene, we repeated the experiments using the 9-tricosene pheromone isomer 7-tricosene (7-T), which contains an identical carbon chain length to 9-tricosene but a double bond at an alternate location. Interestingly, 7-tricosene induced a neutral to slightly repulsive behavior in WT flies (AI = −0.07 ± 0.026, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show wild-type flies exhibited slight repulsion to 7-tricosene (Figure 5—figure supplement 3, AI = -0.07).

claims.claim: Aggregation behavior to the naturally deposited food-odor-induced pheromone depends on 9-tricosene and proper function of the Or7a receptor.
claims.source: These data suggest that aggregation behavior to the naturally deposited food-odor-induced pheromone depends on 9-tricosene and proper function of the Or7a receptor.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on data showing that Or7a mutants and Or7a neuron-ablated flies lack aggregation to both natural pheromone and 9-tricosene, while 7-tricosene (which differs only in double bond position) does not induce aggregation.

claims.claim: A deposited pheromone could guide female egg-laying site selection decisions.
claims.source: Under conditions in which the food-odor-stimulated pheromone was deposited onto the agarose (Figure 6A′), females laid five-fold more eggs in the pheromone quadrant. This suggests that a deposited pheromone could guide female egg-laying site selection decisions.
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show significantly more eggs laid in the pheromone quadrant compared to control quadrants (Figure 6A′, p < 0.001).

claims.claim: Female flies laid significantly more eggs in locations containing only 9-tricosene.
claims.source: We next generated an arena in which one quadrant contained 9-tricosene (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). Female flies also laid significantly more eggs in locations containing only 9-tricosene (Figure 6B′).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show significantly more eggs laid in the 9-tricosene quadrant (Figure 6B′, p < 0.001).

claims.claim: The 9-tricosene egg-laying preference was abolished when Or7a neurons were ablated.
claims.source: The 9-tricosene egg-laying preference was abolished when Or7a neurons were ablated (Or7a-Gal4/UAS-hid or Or7a-Gal4/UAS-DTI) (Figure 6C′ and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or7a neuron-ablated flies showed no significant egg-laying preference for 9-tricosene quadrant (Figure 6C′, p = 0.384; Figure 6—figure supplement 2, p = 0.1349).

claims.claim: The 9-tricosene guided egg laying preference was abolished in Or7a mutant flies.
claims.source: The 9-tricosene guided egg laying preference was also abolished in Or7a mutant flies (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or7a mutants showed no significant egg-laying preference for 9-tricosene (Figure 6D, p = 0.69).

claims.claim: The oviposition preference for the 9-tricosene quadrant was not due to innate attraction to 9-tricosene because females spent similar time in the four quadrants over the 23 hr egg-laying assay.
claims.source: The oviposition preference for the 9-tricosene quadrant was not due to the innate attraction to 9-tricosene because females spent similar time in the four quadrants over the course of the 23 hr egg-laying assay (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: Positional tracking data over 23 hours show no significant positional preference for the 9-tricosene quadrant (Figure 6E, p = 0.1).

claims.claim: Female flies did not preferentially oviposit in the 7-tricosene quadrant.
claims.source: To verify that oviposition guidance is specific to 9-tricosene, we repeated the oviposition experiments using the 9-tricosene pheromone isomer 7-tricosene (7-T), the most abundant cuticular hydrocarbon in male flies (Everaerts et al., 2010). Female flies did not preferentially oviposit in the 7-T quadrant (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show no significant egg-laying preference for 7-tricosene quadrant (Figure 6F, p = 0.28).

claims.claim: Total egg numbers laid were significantly higher in Or7a mutant and Or7a neuron ablated flies.
claims.source: Interestingly, total egg numbers laid were significant higher in Or7a mutant and Or7a neuron ablated flies, implying a potential connection of oviposition site selection and egg deposition number (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show increased total egg numbers in Or7a mutants and Or7a neuron-ablated flies compared to wild-type (Figure 6G, p = 0.0021 and 0.0001).

claims.claim: Or7a is expressed only in the antennae and not in the female ovipositor.
claims.source: However, since Or7a is expressed only in the antennae and not in the female ovipositor (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), this implicates Or7a signaling in the antennae as the main driver of Or7a-directed oviposition guidance.
claims.evidence: Expression analysis shows Or7a-GAL4 expression only in antennae, not in ovipositor or other tissues (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: Or7a signaling in the antennae is the main driver of Or7a-directed oviposition guidance.
claims.source: However, since Or7a is expressed only in the antennae and not in the female ovipositor (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), this implicates Or7a signaling in the antennae as the main driver of Or7a-directed oviposition guidance.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the observation that Or7a is only expressed in antennae, yet Or7a function is necessary for oviposition guidance.

claims.claim: Male derived 9-tricosene can guide female egg-laying preferences, and this decision-making process requires proper antennal Or7a neuronal function.
claims.source: All together, these data suggest that male derived 9-tricosene can guide female egg-laying preferences, and this decision-making process requires proper antennal Or7a neuronal function.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on data showing that 9-tricosene guides oviposition in wild-type but not Or7a mutant or Or7a neuron-ablated flies, and that Or7a is expressed only in antennae.

claims.claim: E2-hexenal was identified as the most potent ligand for Or7a.
claims.source: Comprehensive SSR surveys of odorant–receptor activities identified multiple ligands for the Or7a receptor (Hallem and Carlson, 2006). E2-hexenal, a leafy green volatile released upon fruit or leaf damage (Myung et al., 2006), was identified as the most potent ligand for Or7a (Hallem and Carlson, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to comprehensive characterization studies (Hallem and Carlson, 2006; Myung et al., 2006).

claims.claim: E2-hexenal is a leafy green volatile released upon fruit or leaf damage.
claims.source: E2-hexenal, a leafy green volatile released upon fruit or leaf damage (Myung et al., 2006), was identified as the most potent ligand for Or7a (Hallem and Carlson, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study characterizing E2-hexenal release (Myung et al., 2006).

claims.claim: E2-hexenal directed Or7a-dependent egg-laying site selection.
claims.source: We thus examined if E2-hexenal could direct similar behaviors as those triggered by 9-tricosene (Figure 7, Figure 7—source data 1). Indeed, we found that E2-hexenal, like 9-tricosene, directed Or7a-dependent egg-laying site selection (Figure 7A-D) and attraction (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show E2-hexenal guided egg-laying site selection in wild-type but not Or7a mutant flies (Figure 7C,D).

claims.claim: E2-hexenal directed Or7a-dependent attraction.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that E2-hexenal, like 9-tricosene, directed Or7a-dependent egg-laying site selection (Figure 7A-D) and attraction (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show E2-hexenal elicited attraction in wild-type flies that was significantly reduced in Or7a mutants (Figure 7E, p = 0.0149).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene can effectively guide oviposition in the surrounding presence of low and middle, but not high, E2-hexenal concentrations.
claims.source: To determine if 9-tricosene pheromone cues remained recognizable in a surrounding of E2-hexenal, we repeated the 9-tricosene (10−4 concentration) 3-choice oviposition-selection assays in the presence of high (10−6, 10−7), middle (10−8) or low (10−9,10−10) E2-hexenal concentrations (Figure 7—figure supplement 1). 9-tricosene functioned as an oviposition guidance cue in the presence of low and middle, but not high, E2-hexenal concentrations.
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show 9-tricosene guided oviposition in presence of low and middle E2-hexenal concentrations, but high E2-hexenal concentrations were more potent than 9-tricosene (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: All odorants that activated Or7a directed positive oviposition-site selection to some degree.
claims.source: We therefore tested the oviposition-site selection guidance to 3 additional Or7a-agonists (benzaldeyde, 1-butanol, 1-propanol) as well as 3 odorants that do not activate Or7a (hexyl butyrate, pentanoic acid, ethyl lactate) (Hallem and Carlson, 2006). Interestingly, all odorants that activated Or7a directed positive oviposition-site selection to some degree, whereas all odorants not activating Or7a showed mainly neutral or negative oviposition-site selection effects (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show that Or7a agonists (benzaldehyde, 1-butanol, 1-propanol) all showed positive oviposition preference indices, while non-Or7a agonists showed neutral or negative preferences (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: All odorants not activating Or7a showed mainly neutral or negative oviposition-site selection effects.
claims.source: Interestingly, all odorants that activated Or7a directed positive oviposition-site selection to some degree, whereas all odorants not activating Or7a showed mainly neutral or negative oviposition-site selection effects (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show that non-Or7a agonists (hexyl butyrate, pentanoic acid, ethyl lactate) showed neutral or negative oviposition preference indices (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: Egg-laying site selection was associated with the specificity of the odorant for Or7a: more specific Or7a agonists demonstrated higher positive oviposition site selection.
claims.source: Egg-laying site selection was associated with the specificity of the odorant for Or7a: those odorants (e.g., benzaldehyde or 1-butanol) that activated many additional odorant receptors exhibited decreased oviposition towards that odorant whereas more specific Or7a agonists (e.g., 9-tricosene and 1-propanol) demonstrated the highest positive oviposition site selection (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show correlation between Or7a specificity and oviposition preference, with 9-tricosene and 1-propanol (more specific) showing higher preference than benzaldehyde and 1-butanol (less specific) (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: Selective optogenetic stimulation of Or7a neurons was sufficient to guide egg-laying site selection.
claims.source: Indeed, selective optogenetic stimulation of Or7a neurons was also sufficient to guide egg-laying site selection.
claims.evidence: Optogenetic experiments show that flies fed all-trans-retinal (enabling CsChrimson activation) exhibited significantly increased egg-laying preference for the red light quadrant compared to flies not fed all-trans-retinal (Figure 8—figure supplement 2, p = 0.022).

claims.claim: Or7a neuron activation can influence egg-laying decisions.
claims.source: These results support the findings that Or7a neuron activity can influence egg-laying decisions.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on optogenetic data showing that specific activation of Or7a neurons guides oviposition site selection (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).

claims.claim: Aggregation at a food-site might be strongly influenced by the olfactory perception of an optimal food source.
claims.source: Our results suggest that aggregation at a food-site might be strongly influenced by the olfactory perception of an optimal food source.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on observations that aggregation pheromone is only deposited upon food-odor stimulations (apple cider vinegar, banana, yeast) but not by attractive single components (ethyl acetate).

claims.claim: An aggregation pheromone is only deposited upon food-odor stimulations such as apple cider vinegar, ripe banana and yeast.
claims.source: We found that an aggregation pheromone is only deposited upon food-odor stimulations, such as apple cider vinegar, ripe banana and yeast.
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show post-stimulus aggregation occurs after apple cider vinegar, banana, and yeast stimulation but not after ethyl acetate or humidified air (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).

claims.claim: An attractive odorant component (ethyl acetate) found in apple cider vinegar was not sufficient for pheromone deposition.
claims.source: An attractive odorant component (ethyl acetate) found in apple cider vinegar was not sufficient for pheromone deposition, suggesting that attraction per se to an odor is not sufficient for aggregation pheromone deposition.
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show ethyl acetate was attractive but did not induce post-stimulus aggregation (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).

claims.claim: Attraction per se to an odor is not sufficient for aggregation pheromone deposition.
claims.source: An attractive odorant component (ethyl acetate) found in apple cider vinegar was not sufficient for pheromone deposition, suggesting that attraction per se to an odor is not sufficient for aggregation pheromone deposition.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the observation that ethyl acetate is attractive but does not induce pheromone deposition.

claims.claim: cVA is only weakly attractive on its own.
claims.source: However, in contrast to aggregation pheromones identified in other Drosophila species (Bartelt et al., 1985; Hedlund et al., 1996), cVA is only weakly attractive on its own (Xu et al., 2005), although does enhance aggregation when coupled with food or food-derived odors (Bartelt et al., 1985; Everaerts et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies characterizing cVA attraction properties (Bartelt et al., 1985; Hedlund et al., 1996; Xu et al., 2005; Everaerts et al., 2010).

claims.claim: cVA enhances aggregation when coupled with food or food-derived odors.
claims.source: However, in contrast to aggregation pheromones identified in other Drosophila species (Bartelt et al., 1985; Hedlund et al., 1996), cVA is only weakly attractive on its own (Xu et al., 2005), although does enhance aggregation when coupled with food or food-derived odors (Bartelt et al., 1985; Everaerts et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies showing cVA's role in aggregation with food odors (Bartelt et al., 1985; Everaerts et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Mutating key components in the cVA signaling pathway did not affect the food-odor induced aggregation behavior.
claims.source: However, mutating key components in the cVA signaling pathway did not affect the food-odor induced aggregation behavior.
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show Or67d, lush, and snmp mutants exhibited normal post-stimulus aggregation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).

claims.claim: GC-MS analysis of the active aggregation pheromone extract found no evidence that cVA was deposited.
claims.source: Moreover, GC–MS analysis of the active aggregation pheromone extract found no evidence that cVA was deposited.
claims.evidence: GC-MS data show cVA was not detected in pheromone extracts (Supplementary file 1).

claims.claim: cVA is likely not responsible for the aggregation behaviors triggered by food odors in these experiments.
claims.source: Therefore, cVA is likely not responsible for the aggregation behaviors triggered by food odors in these experiments.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on genetic data showing cVA pathway mutants have normal aggregation, and chemical data showing cVA is not detected in pheromone extracts.

claims.claim: Under natural conditions, cVA may be used as a long distance co-attractant with food odors at mating sites while 9-tricosene is used as a short-range aggregation pheromone at food sites.
claims.source: Nonetheless, it remains possible that under natural conditions, cVA is used as a long distance co-attractant with food odors at mating sites while 9-tricosene is used as a short-range aggregation pheromone at food sites.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the different properties of cVA (volatile, works with food odors) and 9-tricosene (low volatility, food-odor induced).

claims.claim: Pheromone trails play an important role in organizing social foraging behaviors for many flying and non-flying insects.
claims.source: For many flying and non-flying insects, pheromone trails play an important role in organizing social foraging behaviors (Schorkopf et al., 2007; Wyatt, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to reviews on insect pheromone communication (Schorkopf et al., 2007; Wyatt, 2014).

claims.claim: The first animals to find a suitable food source use a pheromone trail to recruit more animals to the food source, establishing a positive feedback of pheromone signaling.
claims.source: The first animals to find a suitable food source use a pheromone trail to recruit even more animals to the food source, which in turn deposit additional pheromone trails, and thereby establish a positive feedback of pheromone signaling towards the foraging site (Schorkopf et al., 2007; Wyatt, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations describing pheromone trail recruitment mechanisms (Schorkopf et al., 2007; Wyatt, 2014).

claims.claim: The experiments identified pheromone tags deposited when D. melanogaster males perceived food odors, implicating the existence of pheromone trail behavior in this insect.
claims.source: Our experiments identified pheromone tags deposited when D. melanogaster males perceived food odors, implicating the existence of such a behavioral occurrence in this insect.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on experimental data showing food-odor-induced pheromone deposition by males that guides aggregation.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene and Or7a neuron activities are likely key mediators of pheromone trail response.
claims.source: We found that 9-tricosene, and Or7a neuron activities, are likely key mediators of this particular pheromone response.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on data showing 9-tricosene is the deposited pheromone and Or7a is necessary and sufficient for its detection and behavioral responses.

claims.claim: The 'E' experiments with 9-tricosene suggest that 9-tricosene may cause repulsion at high concentrations.
claims.source: Interestingly, the 'E' experiments with 9-tricosene suggests that 9-tricosene may cause repulsion at high concentrations, although it remains to be determined if these high concentrations represent natural conditions.
claims.evidence: Behavioral observations from the 'E' pattern experiment show flies avoiding the center of concentrated 9-tricosene deposits (Figure 3F).

claims.claim: E2-hexenal, because of its high volatility, might represent a long-distance cue for recently fallen fruit or plants.
claims.source: E2-hexenal, because of its high volatility, might represent such a long-distance cue for recently fallen fruit or plants.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the known high volatility of E2-hexenal and its release from damaged plant material.

claims.claim: E2-hexenal levels will diminish over extended time periods because it is generated by a plant-dependent enzymatic reaction.
claims.source: Since E2-hexenal is generated by a plant-dependent enzymatic reaction, its levels will diminish over extended time periods (Farag and Pare, 2002q; Myung et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies characterizing E2-hexenal production mechanisms (Farag and Pare, 2002q; Myung et al., 2006).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene, as a low volatility olfactory pheromone, might be ideally suited as a stable close-range olfactory marker to convey environmental conditions.
claims.source: In contrast, 9-tricosene, as a low volatility olfactory pheromone, might be ideally suited as a stable close-range olfactory marker and utilized to convey environmental conditions.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the chemical properties of 9-tricosene (low volatility, stability) and its behavioral functions.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene is a sex attractant for female houseflies (Musca domestica).
claims.source: For instance, 9-tricosene is a sex attractant for female houseflies (Musca domestica) (Carlson et al., 1971) and honey bee waggle dancers (Apis mellifera) use a pheromone cocktail that includes 9-tricosene to communicate with nest mates about the locations of food sources (Thom et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study identifying 9-tricosene function in houseflies (Carlson et al., 1971).

claims.claim: Honey bee waggle dancers (Apis mellifera) use a pheromone cocktail that includes 9-tricosene to communicate with nest mates about the locations of food sources.
claims.source: For instance, 9-tricosene is a sex attractant for female houseflies (Musca domestica) (Carlson et al., 1971) and honey bee waggle dancers (Apis mellifera) use a pheromone cocktail that includes 9-tricosene to communicate with nest mates about the locations of food sources (Thom et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on honey bee communication (Thom et al., 2007).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene represents the first Drosophila cuticular hydrocarbon pheromone demonstrated to activate a Drosophila basiconic sensilla.
claims.source: 9-tricosene represents the first Drosophila cuticular hydrocarbon pheromone that, to our knowledge, is demonstrated to activate a Drosophila basiconic sensilla.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on the novel finding that 9-tricosene activates ab4 basiconic sensilla, contrasting with previous knowledge that pheromones typically activate trichoid sensilla.

claims.claim: The same ab4 sensilla and Or7a olfactory receptor responds to the silk moth pheromone bombykol.
claims.source: Intriguingly, the same sensilla and Or7a olfactory receptor responds to the silk moth pheromone bombykol (Syed et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study showing Or7a responds to bombykol (Syed et al., 2006).

claims.claim: The Drosophila Or7a neuron's response to bombykol might represent off-target ligand specificity for 9-tricosene.
claims.source: It is interesting to speculate that this Drosophila neuron's response to bombykol might represent off-target ligand specificity for 9-tricosene.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that Or7a responds to both 9-tricosene and bombykol.

claims.claim: Activation of odorant receptors by both pheromone and plant volatiles might be more widespread than previously anticipated.
claims.source: Our data further suggests that activation of odorant receptors by both pheromone and plant volatiles might be more widespread than previously anticipated.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the finding that Or7a responds to both the pheromone 9-tricosene and the plant volatile E2-hexenal, and is supported by a citation showing a moth pheromone receptor also responds to a plant volatile (Rouyar et al., 2015).

claims.claim: An olfactory receptor in the moth Agrotis ipsilon that was previously considered pheromone specific was recently found to also respond to the plant volatile heptanal.
claims.source: Indeed, an olfactory receptor in the moth Agrotis ipsilon that was previously considered to be pheromone specific was recently found to also respond to the plant volatile heptanal, despite the plant volatile showing no structural similarity to the moth pheromone (Rouyar et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent study on moth olfactory receptors (Rouyar et al., 2015).

claims.claim: Oviposition site selection comprises three steps: an ovipositor motor program, a clean/rest period and a search-like behavior.
claims.source: The behavior comprises three steps—an ovipositor motor program, a clean/rest period and a search-like behavior.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study characterizing oviposition behavior (Yang et al., 2008).

claims.claim: The ovipositor motor program that leads to egg deposition is relatively short (6-7 s) compared to clean/rest and search-like behaviors (100-130 s).
claims.source: The ovipositor motor program that leads to egg deposition is relatively short (6–7 s) as compared to clean/rest and search-like behaviors (100–130 s) (Yang et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study quantifying oviposition behavior timing (Yang et al., 2008).

claims.claim: 9-tricosene might mediate two temporally distinct responses: a short-term aggregation behavior lasting ~25 min and a long-term oviposition site selection behavior lasting for hours.
claims.source: These findings also suggest that 9-tricosene might mediate two temporally distinct responses in our experimental design. A short-term aggregation behavior that lasts ∼25 min and a long-term oviposition site selection behavior that lasts for hours.
claims.evidence: This speculation is based on observations that aggregation lasts ~25 min while oviposition preference persists for 23 hours without positional preference.

claims.claim: A possible mechanism underlying different temporal behaviors could be that detection thresholds for the two behaviors are different, with higher 9-tricosene concentrations triggering aggregation and low concentrations affecting oviposition.
claims.source: A possible mechanism underlying these different behaviors could be that detection thresholds for the two behaviors are different, that is, higher concentrations of 9-tricosene triggers aggregation whereas low 9-tricosene concentrations affect oviposition.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms for the observed temporal differences in behavior.

claims.claim: In many insects, eggs are vulnerable and larvae have restricted motility, thus oviposition site selection is a crucial decision for progeny survival.
claims.source: In many insects, eggs are vulnerable and larvae have restricted motility, thus oviposition site selection is a crucial decision for progeny survival.
claims.evidence: This is general knowledge about insect biology and the importance of oviposition decisions.

claims.claim: The hypothesis of 'mother-knows-best' stipulates that female egg-laying decisions evolved to oviposit in places offering the best survival of offspring.
claims.source: The hypothesis of 'mother-knows-best' stipulates that female egg-laying decisions evolved to oviposit in places offering the best survival of offspring (Soto et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on oviposition decision-making (Soto et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Oviposition decisions require multiple sensory modalities, such as visual, olfactory, gustatory and proprioception.
claims.source: As expected, oviposition decisions require multiple sensory modalities, such as visual, olfactory, gustatory and proprioception (Yang et al., 2008; Joseph et al., 2009; Schwartz et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies characterizing sensory inputs to oviposition (Yang et al., 2008; Joseph et al., 2009; Schwartz et al., 2012).

claims.claim: A previously considered female-only decision (oviposition) can be modulated by a male-deposited pheromone.
claims.source: Our study shows that a previously considered female-only decision can in fact be modulated by a male-deposited pheromone.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on data showing that male-deposited 9-tricosene guides female oviposition decisions.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene could be a mechanism used by Drosophila males to increase the likelihood that their progeny will be laid in an optimal location.
claims.source: Since 9-tricosene is enriched only upon food-odor stimulation, and acts to aggregate animals and increase courtship (Lin and Potter, unpublished observations), it could be a mechanism used by Drosophila males to increase the likelihood that their progeny will be laid in an optimal location.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the observed properties of 9-tricosene (food-odor induced, guides oviposition, increases courtship).

claims.claim: In addition to 'mother-knows-best', 'father' may have co-opted a female's olfactory system to influence egg-laying decisions for maximizing progeny survival.
claims.source: Thus, in addition to 'mother-knows-best', this suggest that 'father' may have co-opted a female's olfactory system in order to influence an egg-laying decision for maximizing progeny survival.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the finding that male-deposited pheromone influences female oviposition decisions.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene is a specific activator of Or7a, but Or7a is not activated only by 9-tricosene.
claims.source: 9-Tricosene is a specific activator of Or7a, but Or7a is not activated only by 9-tricosene.
claims.evidence: This is based on electrophysiological data showing 9-tricosene specifically activates Or7a, combined with previous knowledge that Or7a responds to many odorants.

claims.claim: There is a strong positive correlation between the specificity of Or7a activation and oviposition-guidance.
claims.source: Our behavioral experiments suggest a strong positive correlation with the specificity of Or7a activation and oviposition-guidance.
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show that more specific Or7a agonists (9-tricosene, 1-propanol) elicit stronger oviposition preferences than less specific agonists (benzaldehyde, 1-butanol) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: Activation of the Or7a olfactory receptor neuron can strongly influence egg-laying decisions.
claims.source: This suggests that activation of the Or7a olfactory receptor neuron can strongly influence egg-laying decisions.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on behavioral data showing Or7a agonists guide oviposition and optogenetic activation of Or7a neurons is sufficient to guide oviposition.

claims.claim: 9-tricosene may have a specific influence on oviposition decisions due to its specific activation of Or7a.
claims.source: 9-Tricosense may therefore have a specific influence on oviposition decisions due to its specific activation of Or7a.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the observation that 9-tricosene specifically activates Or7a and that Or7a activation influences oviposition.

claims.claim: Or7a olfactory neurons join a growing list of olfactory neurons found to mediate specific olfactory behaviors.
claims.source: Or7a olfactory neurons join a growing list of olfactory neurons found to mediate specific olfactory behaviors like oviposition-site selection (Dweck et al., 2013, 2015b), aversion (Suh et al., 2004; Ai et al., 2010; Stensmyr et al., 2012), courtship (Kurtovic et al., 2007), and attraction (Semmelhack and Wang, 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies identifying specific olfactory neurons mediating specific behaviors.

claims.claim: Odorants besides 9-tricosene that stimulate Or7a neurons will activate additional olfactory receptor neurons that may function to mask or modulate Or7a-mediated egg-laying behaviors.
claims.source: Odorants besides 9-tricosene that stimulate Or7a neurons will activate additional olfactory receptor neurons that may function to mask or modulate Or7a-mediated egg-laying behaviors.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the observation that less specific Or7a agonists (which activate other receptors) show reduced oviposition guidance compared to specific agonists.

claims.claim: Olfactory systems function to make sense of a complex environment by assigning biological weights and values to different olfactory neuron activity patterns that together influence a behavioral choice.
claims.source: This likely reflects how olfactory systems function to make sense of a complex environment, by assigning biological weights and values to different olfactory neuron activity patterns that together influence a behavioral choice.
claims.evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the observed data on how Or7a and other olfactory neurons influence behavior.

claims.claim: Food odors and pheromone signals project to non-overlapping divisions in higher brain regions in Drosophila.
claims.source: Food odors and pheromone signals have been shown to project to non-overlapping divisions in higher brain regions in Drosophila, suggesting that distinct brain divisions may be involved in mediating different biological functions (Jefferis et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on olfactory projection patterns (Jefferis et al., 2007).

claims.claim: Basiconic Or7a neurons are responsible for 9-tricosene and E2-hexenal guided oviposition decisions.
claims.source: We demonstrate that basiconic Or7a neurons are responsible for 9-tricosene and E2-hexenal guided oviposition decisions (Figure 6C,D,7C,7D).
claims.evidence: Behavioral data show that Or7a mutants and Or7a neuron-ablated flies lack oviposition preference for both 9-tricosene and E2-hexenal (Figures 6C,D and 7C,D).

claims.claim: Flies prefer citrus fruit as oviposition substrates as detected by Or19a+ olfactory neurons.
claims.source: Recently, it was found that flies preferred citrus fruit as oviposition substrates as detected by Or19a + olfactory neurons (Dweck et al., 2013), and also preferred to oviposit on substrates containing ethylphenols as detected by Or71a + olfactory neurons (Dweck et al., 2015b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies identifying Or19a and Or71a roles in oviposition (Dweck et al., 2013, 2015b).

claims.claim: Flies prefer to oviposit on substrates containing ethylphenols as detected by Or71a+ olfactory neurons.
claims.source: Recently, it was found that flies preferred citrus fruit as oviposition substrates as detected by Or19a + olfactory neurons (Dweck et al., 2013), and also preferred to oviposit on substrates containing ethylphenols as detected by Or71a + olfactory neurons (Dweck et al., 2015b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on Or71a and oviposition (Dweck et al., 2015b).

claims.claim: The Or7a DL5, Or19a DC1, and Or71a VC2 projection neurons share highly similar axonal projection patterns in the lateral horn that are distinct from previously described food and pheromone regions.
claims.source: Interestingly, the Or7a DL5, Or19a DC1, and Or71a VC2 projection neurons share highly similar axonal projection patterns in the lateral horn that are distinct from previously described food and pheromone regions (Jefferis et al., 2007; Ronderos et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to studies characterizing projection neuron anatomy (Jefferis et al., 2007; Ronderos et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Oviposition site-selection might be strongly guided by a dedicated olfactory processing brain center.
claims.source: This suggests that oviposition site-selection might be strongly guided by a dedicated olfactory processing brain center.
claims.evidence: This inference is based on the observation that multiple olfactory neurons guiding oviposition (Or7a, Or19a, Or71a) project to similar regions in the lateral horn.

results.result: Drosophila exhibit post-stimulus aggregation behavior after apple cider vinegar exposure that is not due to residual odor on glass plates or passive crowding, suggesting specific pheromone deposition in response to food odor.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C18 provide converging evidence through behavioral tracking (C15), control experiments ruling out residual odor (C16) and passive deposition via humidified air attraction (C17), supporting the inference of food-odor-specific pheromone deposition (C18). The experimental controls are appropriate and the conclusion is logically supported.

results.result: Post-stimulus aggregation is induced by complex food odors (apple cider vinegar, banana, yeast) but not by attractive single components like ethyl acetate, suggesting specificity for food odor perception rather than attraction per se.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C21 demonstrate that complex food odors induce post-stimulus aggregation while an attractive single component does not, supporting the inference that food odor complexity or perception, not mere attraction, triggers pheromone deposition. The experimental design appropriately tests this distinction.

results.result: Male flies are the source of the aggregation pheromone, which is equally attractive to both virgin and mated males and females.
results.evaluation: Claim C22 is supported by experiments using different depositor fly combinations showing only males produce the pheromone (Figure 1I, p=0.003). Claim C23 shows similar aggregation across sex and mating status (Figure 1—figure supplement 8). The experimental design appropriately isolates the source and tests detector responses.

results.result: Detection of the food-odor-induced pheromone requires the orco-dependent olfactory system but not gustatory receptors, ppk23, or most ionotropic receptors. Orco mutants show repulsion due to residual acetic acid detection via Ir8a/Ir64a.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C33 systematically test different chemosensory pathways using appropriate mutants. The data show orco is necessary (C28, C33) while other pathways are not (C24-C27). The repulsion phenotype in orco mutants is explained by acid sensing (C29-C31) with appropriate controls (neutralized vinegar, double mutants). The logic and experimental design are sound.

results.result: cVA is not the food-odor induced aggregation pheromone, as demonstrated by normal aggregation in cVA pathway mutants and absence of cVA in GC-MS analysis of pheromone extracts.
results.evaluation: Claims C34, C100-C102 provide genetic evidence (Or67d, lush, snmp mutants show normal aggregation) and chemical evidence (GC-MS does not detect cVA) that converge to exclude cVA as the pheromone. Claim C38 provides additional chemical confirmation. The conclusion is well-supported by multiple independent lines of evidence.

results.result: The aggregation pheromone can be extracted with hexane and is volatile, as demonstrated by flies tracing hexane-painted patterns and behavioral responses to heating and air flushing.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C37 demonstrate extractability (C36: flies follow 'E' patterns painted with hexane extracts) and volatility (C37: multiple lines of evidence including olfactory requirement, reduction over time with air flushing, and elimination with heating). The experimental approaches appropriately test these chemical properties.

results.result: GC-MS analysis identified 9-tricosene as significantly enriched (2.8-fold) in food-odor stimulated conditions compared to controls, while other cuticular hydrocarbons were absent or present at trace amounts.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C42 report GC-MS results showing 9-tricosene enrichment with appropriate controls (apple cider vinegar only, humidified air + flies). The exclusion of 7-tricosene (C41) is supported by both chemical data and behavioral data from ppk23 mutants. The analytical approach is appropriate for pheromone identification.

results.result: 9-tricosene elicits dose-dependent attraction and guides aggregation behaviors, though flies avoid concentrated deposits, suggesting it functions as an aggregation pheromone under certain conditions with possible additional components contributing to the full phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C47 show 9-tricosene is attractive (C44: Figure 3D-E) and guides aggregation (C45: 'E' pattern following), but with caveats about concentration-dependent repulsion (C46) and incomplete recapitulation of natural pheromone behavior (C47). The conclusion appropriately acknowledges limitations while supporting the main finding.

results.result: Oenocyte-derived cuticular hydrocarbons are essential for post-stimulus aggregation, as demonstrated by loss of aggregation when oenocyte-ablated males are used as depositors.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C50 use oenocyte ablation to test the requirement for cuticular hydrocarbons. The data show reduced aggregation (Figure 3—figure supplement 4, p=0.0021) when oenocyte-ablated males are depositors. This genetic approach appropriately tests the cellular source of the pheromone, consistent with 9-tricosene being an oenocyte-derived cuticular hydrocarbon.

results.result: 9-tricosene activates an orco-dependent odorant receptor and does not require Ir or Gr receptors, as demonstrated by complete loss of EAG responses in orco mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C52 use electroantennogram recordings to show orco mutants lack 9-tricosene responses (Figure 4A,B). This electrophysiological approach appropriately demonstrates orco-dependence at the antennal level, complementing the behavioral data. The inference that Ir/Gr receptors are not required is logically supported.

results.result: 9-tricosene specifically activates the ab4A neurons expressing Or7a receptors in basiconic sensilla, as demonstrated by single sensillum recordings showing robust responses in the larger amplitude neuron of ab4.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C55 use single sensillum recordings to identify ab4 as responsive (C53: Figure 4C) and specifically the ab4A/Or7a neuron based on spike amplitude (C54). Claim C55 shows increased ab4A activation with flies pre-exposed to apple cider vinegar (p=0.03). The electrophysiological identification is appropriate and well-controlled.

results.result: Or7a is sufficient for 9-tricosene responses, as demonstrated by misexpression of Or7a in ab3A neurons conferring 9-tricosene responsiveness comparable to native ab4 neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C58 use receptor misexpression to demonstrate sufficiency. The data show ab3 neurons expressing Or7a respond to 9-tricosene similarly to native ab4 neurons (Figure 4D,E). This gain-of-function approach appropriately demonstrates sufficiency, complementing the necessity data from mutants.

results.result: Or7a is necessary for 9-tricosene activation in ab4 sensilla, as demonstrated by complete loss of ab4A spiking activity in Or7a mutants while ab4B responses to geosmin remain intact.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C63 use Or7a mutants to demonstrate necessity. The data show no ab4A response to 9-tricosene in mutants while ab4B/Or56a responses to geosmin are preserved (Figure 4F,G), providing an internal control. This loss-of-function approach with appropriate controls strongly supports necessity.

results.result: 9-tricosene specifically activates the broadly tuned 'generalist' Or7a receptor, which responds to many aldehydes and alcohols, representing an unexpected finding for pheromone detection.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C56, C64 establish that Or7a is both necessary and sufficient for 9-tricosene detection (supported by C51-C63) while also being broadly tuned to many odorants (C56: citations to Hallem et al., 2004; Hallem and Carlson, 2006). This represents a novel finding that a pheromone activates a generalist receptor, contrasting with previous pheromone receptors.

results.result: Or7a-GAL4 drives expression specifically in olfactory neurons targeting the DL5 antennal lobe glomerulus, with no expression detected outside the antennae.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C66 characterize the Or7a-GAL4 expression pattern using immunostaining (Figure 5A) and whole-animal imaging (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The data show specific DL5 innervation consistent with previous characterization (Couto et al., 2005) and no extra-antennal expression. This anatomical characterization is appropriate for subsequent functional studies.

results.result: Or7a neurons and Or7a receptor are necessary for aggregation responses to both naturally deposited pheromone and 9-tricosene, as demonstrated by complete loss of attraction in Or7a neuron-ablated flies and Or7a mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C68, C70-C71 use both neuronal ablation (Or7a-Gal4/UAS-hid, Or7a-Gal4/UAS-DTI) and receptor mutation to demonstrate necessity for aggregation to natural pheromone and 9-tricosene (Figure 5B-E). The convergence of genetic ablation and mutation approaches strongly supports the requirement for Or7a in aggregation behavior.

results.result: Ablation of other odorant receptors (Or83c, Or43a, Or88a) does not affect aggregation, demonstrating specificity for Or7a.
results.evaluation: Claim C69 provides specificity controls showing that ablating other odorant receptor neurons does not affect aggregation (Figure 5C). This control is essential for demonstrating that the Or7a requirement is specific and not a general effect of olfactory neuron ablation.

results.result: Aggregation behavior is specific to 9-tricosene, as the isomer 7-tricosene induces neutral to slightly repulsive behavior, and aggregation depends on proper Or7a function.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C73 use the structural isomer 7-tricosene as a specificity control, showing it does not induce aggregation (Figure 5—figure supplement 3, AI=-0.07). This control appropriately demonstrates that aggregation is specific to 9-tricosene structure and Or7a function, not just any tricosene.

results.result: Male-deposited pheromone and 9-tricosene guide female egg-laying site selection, with females laying five-fold more eggs in pheromone-containing quadrants.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C75 demonstrate oviposition guidance using modified arenas with agarose substrates. The data show significantly more eggs in pheromone (Figure 6A′, p<0.001) and 9-tricosene quadrants (Figure 6B′, p<0.001). The experimental design appropriately tests oviposition site selection with only mated females to avoid confounding male effects.

results.result: Or7a neurons and Or7a receptor are necessary for 9-tricosene-guided oviposition site selection, as demonstrated by loss of egg-laying preference in Or7a neuron-ablated flies and Or7a mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C77 use neuronal ablation and receptor mutation to demonstrate Or7a requirement for oviposition guidance. The data show loss of preference in Or7a-Gal4/UAS-hid (Figure 6C′, p=0.384), Or7a-Gal4/UAS-DTI (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, p=0.1349), and Or7a mutants (Figure 6D, p=0.69). The convergence of approaches strongly supports necessity.

results.result: Oviposition preference for 9-tricosene is not due to innate attraction, as females spend similar time in all quadrants over the 23-hour assay period.
results.evaluation: Claim C78 uses positional tracking over 23 hours to distinguish oviposition site selection from positional preference. The data show no significant positional bias (Figure 6E, p=0.1) despite egg-laying preference, demonstrating that oviposition guidance is a specific decision distinct from general attraction. This control is important for interpreting the behavioral mechanism.

results.result: Oviposition guidance is specific to 9-tricosene, as females do not preferentially oviposit in 7-tricosene quadrants despite 7-tricosene being the most abundant male cuticular hydrocarbon.
results.evaluation: Claim C79 uses 7-tricosene as a specificity control for oviposition, showing no preference (Figure 6F, p=0.28). This control appropriately demonstrates that oviposition guidance is specific to 9-tricosene structure, not just any abundant male cuticular hydrocarbon, ruling out a general hydrocarbon nutritional effect.

results.result: Or7a mutant and Or7a neuron-ablated flies lay significantly more total eggs, and since Or7a is expressed only in antennae (not ovipositor), antennal Or7a signaling is the main driver of oviposition guidance.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C82 show increased total egg numbers in Or7a mutants and ablated flies (Figure 6G, p=0.0021 and 0.0001), and that Or7a expression is antennal-specific (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The inference that antennal Or7a drives oviposition guidance is logically supported by the expression pattern, though the increased egg number phenotype suggests additional complexity in Or7a function.

results.result: E2-hexenal, the most potent Or7a ligand, directs Or7a-dependent egg-laying site selection and attraction similar to 9-tricosene.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C87 show E2-hexenal guides oviposition in wild-type but not Or7a mutants (Figure 7C,D) and elicits Or7a-dependent attraction (Figure 7E, p=0.0149). This demonstrates that Or7a activation by different ligands can guide similar behaviors, supporting the hypothesis that Or7a neuron activity influences oviposition decisions.

results.result: 9-tricosene can effectively guide oviposition in the presence of low and middle E2-hexenal concentrations, but high E2-hexenal concentrations are more potent than 9-tricosene.
results.evaluation: Claim C88 tests whether 9-tricosene pheromone signals remain detectable in the presence of E2-hexenal, a potentially abundant Or7a agonist. The data show 9-tricosene functions at low/middle E2-hexenal concentrations but not high concentrations (Figure 7—figure supplement 1). This appropriately addresses ecological relevance and demonstrates concentration-dependent competition between Or7a ligands.

results.result: All Or7a agonists tested (benzaldehyde, 1-butanol, 1-propanol) directed positive oviposition site selection, while non-Or7a agonists showed neutral or negative effects. Oviposition preference correlates with Or7a specificity, with more specific agonists showing stronger preferences.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C91 systematically test multiple Or7a agonists and non-agonists for oviposition guidance (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1). The data show a clear pattern: Or7a agonists guide positive oviposition while non-agonists do not, and specificity correlates with preference strength. This comprehensive approach strongly supports the hypothesis that Or7a activation influences oviposition decisions.

results.result: Selective optogenetic stimulation of Or7a neurons is sufficient to guide egg-laying site selection, demonstrating that Or7a neuron activation can influence oviposition decisions.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C93 use optogenetics (Or7a-GAL4; UAS-CsChrimson) to demonstrate sufficiency of Or7a neuron activation for oviposition guidance. The data show increased egg-laying preference for red light quadrants in flies fed all-trans-retinal versus controls (Figure 8—figure supplement 2, p=0.022). This gain-of-function approach complements the loss-of-function and ligand studies, strongly supporting that Or7a activity drives oviposition decisions.

results.result: Male Drosophila deposit 9-tricosene upon apple cider vinegar stimulation, which functions as both an aggregation pheromone and oviposition guidance cue, linking food-odor perception with aggregation and egg-laying decisions via Or7a.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C14 represent the main findings of the manuscript, integrating pheromone identification (C1: GC-MS, behavioral data), aggregation function (C2: behavioral assays), oviposition function (C3: egg-laying assays), and mechanistic link via Or7a (C14). These claims are supported by the comprehensive set of chemical, electrophysiological, genetic, and behavioral data presented throughout the manuscript.

results.result: Or7a is activated by many alcohols and aldehydes including E2-hexenal, a leafy green volatile released upon fruit or leaf damage, which was previously identified as the most potent Or7a ligand.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C84-C85 are supported by citations to comprehensive characterization studies (Hallem and Carlson, 2006; Myung et al., 2006). These prior work claims provide important context for understanding Or7a as a broadly tuned receptor and the ecological relevance of E2-hexenal as an Or7a ligand.

results.result: Loss of Or7a neurons or Or7a receptor abolishes aggregation behavior and oviposition site-selection towards both 9-tricosene and E2-hexenal.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C13 summarize the necessity of Or7a for behavioral responses to both 9-tricosene and E2-hexenal, encompassing both aggregation and oviposition behaviors. These claims are supported by the detailed behavioral data from neuronal ablation and receptor mutation experiments (Figures 5-7), demonstrating comprehensive Or7a requirement across ligands and behaviors.

results.result: 9-tricosene is a male-specific volatile pheromone in D. melanogaster and other insects, with cVA being only weakly attractive on its own but enhancing aggregation when coupled with food odors. Under natural conditions, cVA and 9-tricosene may serve different spatial roles.
results.evaluation: Claims C43, C98-C99, C103, C112-C113 provide context from prior work on 9-tricosene and cVA functions in Drosophila and other insects. These are appropriately cited claims (Everaerts et al., 2010; Farine et al., 2012; Bartelt et al., 1985; Xu et al., 2005; Carlson et al., 1971; Thom et al., 2007) that contextualize the current findings. Claim C103 is speculation about natural conditions.

results.result: Aggregation at food sites is influenced by olfactory perception of optimal food sources, with aggregation pheromone deposited only upon food-odor stimulations (not attractive single components), suggesting attraction alone is insufficient for pheromone deposition.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C97 synthesize the findings on food-odor specificity of pheromone deposition. The inference that food-odor perception (not mere attraction) triggers deposition is supported by the differential responses to complex food odors versus ethyl acetate (Figure 1—figure supplement 7). This represents an important mechanistic insight into pheromone deposition control.

results.result: Pheromone trails organize social foraging in many insects through positive feedback recruitment. The current experiments identify such pheromone tags in D. melanogaster, with 9-tricosene and Or7a as key mediators.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 provide general knowledge context (citations to Schorkopf et al., 2007; Wyatt, 2014) about pheromone trail behavior. Claims C106-C107 appropriately connect the current findings to this broader context, inferring that the observed food-odor-induced pheromone deposition represents pheromone trail behavior in Drosophila. The inference is reasonable given the data.

results.result: 9-tricosene represents the first Drosophila cuticular hydrocarbon pheromone demonstrated to activate basiconic sensilla. Or7a also responds to silk moth pheromone bombykol, and dual pheromone/plant volatile activation may be more widespread than anticipated.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C118 discuss the novelty and broader implications of the findings. C114 correctly identifies this as the first cuticular hydrocarbon activating basiconic sensilla. C115-C116 note Or7a's response to bombykol (Syed et al., 2006) and speculate on off-target specificity. C117-C118 appropriately generalize to other systems (Rouyar et al., 2015). These claims represent valid contextualization and speculation based on the data.

results.result: Oviposition comprises three behavioral steps with different timescales. 9-tricosene may mediate two temporally distinct responses: short-term aggregation (~25 min) and long-term oviposition site selection (hours), possibly through different detection thresholds.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C120 cite prior work on oviposition behavior timing (Yang et al., 2008). Claims C121-C122 speculate about mechanisms underlying the observed temporal differences between aggregation and oviposition behaviors. While the speculation is reasonable given the data, it remains untested. The temporal distinction is observed but the threshold mechanism is speculative.

results.result: Oviposition site selection is crucial for progeny survival and requires multiple sensory modalities. The current study shows this 'female-only' decision can be modulated by male-deposited pheromone, suggesting males may influence egg-laying decisions to maximize progeny survival.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C125 provide appropriate context from prior work on oviposition biology and the 'mother-knows-best' hypothesis. Claims C126-C128 appropriately connect the current findings to this framework, with C127-C128 representing reasonable speculation about adaptive significance. The main finding (C126) that male pheromone influences oviposition is well-supported by the data.

results.result: 9-tricosene specifically activates Or7a, but Or7a responds to many odorants. Oviposition guidance correlates with Or7a activation specificity, suggesting Or7a neuron activation strongly influences egg-laying decisions, with 9-tricosene having specific influence due to its Or7a specificity.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C132 synthesize the findings on Or7a specificity and behavioral consequences. The correlation between Or7a specificity and oviposition strength (C130: Figure 8—figure supplement 1) supports the inference that Or7a activation influences oviposition (C131), with 9-tricosene's specificity conferring specific influence (C132). The logic is sound and supported by the systematic odorant testing.

results.result: Or7a neurons join a growing list of olfactory neurons mediating specific behaviors. Odorants activating Or7a plus other receptors may mask Or7a-mediated behaviors, reflecting how olfactory systems assign biological weights to neuron activity patterns to influence behavioral choices.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C135 appropriately contextualize the findings within broader olfactory neuroscience (C133: citations to multiple studies). Claims C134-C135 provide reasonable inferences about how olfactory coding works based on the observed correlation between Or7a specificity and behavioral strength. These represent valid generalizations from the data.

results.result: Or7a, Or19a, and Or71a neurons all guide oviposition site selection and share similar lateral horn projection patterns distinct from food and pheromone regions, suggesting oviposition may be guided by a dedicated olfactory processing brain center.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C139 establish that multiple olfactory neurons (Or7a, Or19a, Or71a) guide oviposition (current data and citations to Dweck et al., 2013, 2015b). Claim C140 notes their similar lateral horn projections (citations to Jefferis et al., 2007; Ronderos et al., 2014). Claim C141 appropriately infers a dedicated oviposition processing center. The inference is reasonable given the anatomical convergence.

results.result: 9-tricosene may cause repulsion at high concentrations. E2-hexenal's high volatility may represent a long-distance cue for damaged fruit, with levels diminishing over time, while 9-tricosene's low volatility makes it suited as a stable close-range marker.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C111 represent speculation about ecological functions and chemical properties. C108 is based on observation from 'E' experiments but ecological relevance is uncertain. C109-C111 speculate about E2-hexenal and 9-tricosene functions based on their chemical properties and known biology (citations to Farag and Pare, 2002q; Myung et al., 2006). While reasonable, these remain speculative hypotheses requiring further testing.

results.result: Basiconic sensilla were traditionally considered food odor detectors. Both male and female ab4A/Or7a neurons respond equally to 9-tricosene, consistent with attraction to both sexes, and Or7a neurons do not respond to cVA.
results.evaluation: Claim C59 provides appropriate context (citations to multiple studies). Claim C60 shows sex-independent Or7a responses (Figure 4E) consistent with behavioral data. Claim C61 shows no cVA response (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), consistent with cVA not being the pheromone. These claims appropriately characterize Or7a neuron properties.
